thread:
maria: quick follow-up from the authn/authz sync  we need to settle on a canonical namespace binding for service tokens. current state: some proxies expect `org:project` in `sub`, others read `claims.namespace`. We should pick one and define a stable encoding for service claims (audience, routing hints, short-lived metadata).
kevin: +1 we need one clear field. my vote is a single `namespace` claim with `org/project` string, and keep `aud` for runtime audience. simpler for routers.
olivia: worry: some downstreams rely on project-less org tokens and the reverse. If we force `org/project` we'll need migration compatibility. also token size matters for headers.
maria: good point. migration needs to be explicit. options: 1) keep `sub` as-is and add `namespace` (new); 2) repurpose `sub` to canonical form; 3) introduce `namespaces` array to support multi-affinity. pros/cons?
sam: prefer option 1 for smooth rollout. Add `namespace` claim, and have a short `ns_hash` for header routing to keep header size small. routers can prefer `namespace` then fallback to `sub` parsing.
kevin: agree. also we should pick encoding: JWT claim as string vs protobuf-encoded base64 blob. JWT string is easiest for everyone. proto blob is compact but opaque to simple proxies.
olivia: proto blob would let us include richer metadata (rollout tags, region hints) without polluting top-level claims. but then older proxies can't read it.
kevin: can we do both? keep top-level lightweight claims (`namespace`, `aud`, `exp`, `ns_hash`) and an optional `x-meta` base64 proto for richer fields. that gives forward path.
maria: sounds sensible. need to define `ns_hash` algorithm and collision semantics. recommend short 6 hex chars derived from sha256(namespace) truncated. used only for fast header routing, not authoritative.
sam: +1. TTL: we should standardize service tokens to <= 1h by default, with short-lived refresh for long-running jobs. for probes/cert-based tokens allow longer but instrument heavily.
olivia: about audience: we have long lists of compatible services. use `aud` array with canonical names, and add `route_hint` claim (single string) for best-effort routing.
kevin: sample claim draft:

```
{
  "iss": "auth.redwood",
  "sub": "svc:billing:ingest", // legacy format kept for compat
  "namespace": "billing-team/ingest", 
  "ns_hash": "a1b2c3",
  "aud": ["inference-gateway","metrics"],
  "exp": 1712345678,
  "route_hint": "eu-west-1",
  "x-meta": "<base64 proto>"
}
```

sam: also add `binding_type` claim: `service`, `agent`, `user` — helps authorize proxies to enforce different rules.
maria: migration plan bullets: 1) publish schema + code samples; 2) rollout auth server v2 emitting `namespace` and `ns_hash` (dual-write `sub` for 3 months); 3) update internal routers to prefer `namespace` and log fallbacks; 4) sunset parsing of non-canonical subs after metrics show <1% fallback for 90 days; 5) enforce `binding_type` for new issuance.
olivia: we should add a warning header when proxies fallback to `sub` to track where old parsing exists. e.g., `X-Auth-Fallback: sub` in logs.
kevin: tests: add unit tests parsing both forms, fuzz `ns_hash` collisions, and e2e with ingress gateways. perf: ensure header size impact < 200 bytes; `x-meta` optional.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: auth-service/v2 will be deployed to canary today 11:30 UTC -> will emit both claims. Rollout scheduled 2 weeks.
maria: thanks — can someone put this into an RFC follow-up doc? want a short formal schema + examples + migration checklist.
sam: i'll draft the RFC addendum and ping infra for router changes. tagging @olivia for perf/security review.
kevin: i'll add unit tests and sample parser helpers to the auth SDK.
olivia: i'll write compatibility test matrix and the fallback-logging plan.
maria: perfect. closing thread for now — will sync in 1:1 if blockers.
